title: 3-Year Treasury Note auction (December new issue) — stops Monday 1:00pm ET, two days before the 12-09 FOMC decision
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), FlateDecode streams inflated PER PAGE and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates. The page-3 row reads verbatim `3-Year NOTE / Thursday, December 03, 2026 / Monday, December 07, 2026 / Tuesday, December 15, 2026`, with no `R` and no `T` marker — a NEW ISSUE, matching `reopening: "No"` on every 3-Year row in fiscaldata `auctions_query`. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-03 coupon announcement. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICALISED 2026-09-09 from `proposals/treasury-3y-note-2026-12-07.from-treasury-3y-note-2026-11-09.json` (the only proposal for this id), whose date, new-issue read and settle date all reproduce against a fresh page-by-page fetch of the same primary. FOUR AMENDMENTS to what the proposal carried. (1) THE BLOCK STEPS AROUND FOMC, THE BILL CALENDAR DOES NOT. The proposal's structural note says 'nothing on Wednesday 12-09'. The same PDF page shows a 17-Week BILL announced 12-08 and auctioned WEDNESDAY 12-09. What is empty on FOMC day is the COUPON slate, not the calendar. (2) THE DECEMBER MONDAY IS FOMC-DRIVEN, WHICH NARROWS THE NOVEMBER SIBLING. That ledger cited the December and January Mondays as evidence the slot is 'a scheduling pattern rather than a Veterans-Day artifact'. Measured over the 213 monthly-cadence auctions since 2009: all 7 December 3-Years that sold on a MONDAY had the FOMC decision in the SAME WEEK (D-1 or D-2) — 2011, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2025 — while 9 of the 10 December Tuesdays had it 7-8 days out. The converse fails once (2012-12-11, a Tuesday at D-1), so the rule is one-directional and stated that way. 2026 is the Monday/D-2 shape, and its nearest analogue is 2025-12-08: Monday, D-2, $58B, bid-to-cover 2.640. (3) THE SERIES IS LONGER THAN THE SIBLINGS RECORD. `auctions_query` returns `total-count: 300` on ONE page back to 1981-05-05; the '200 rows back to 2010-02-09, the full series the endpoint carries' in the September/October/November ledgers is a page-size artifact, not the endpoint's limit. This doc uses the 213 rows from 2009-01-07 (where the monthly cadence starts) and says so. (4) THIS IS A MID-QUARTER BLOCK, NOT A REFUNDING ONE: the December 10-Year (12-08) and 30-Year (12-10) both carry `R` — reopenings — where November's three legs were all new issues. That is exactly the comparison the November sibling measured to a null (refunding vs mid-quarter bid-to-cover t = 0.96), which is what licenses transferring its base rates here untouched. EXPECTED SIZE, from the grid rather than any published document: $58B, which would be the 33rd consecutive $58B new issue since 2024-04-09 — 30 are completed through 2026-09-08 (`auctions_query`, re-pulled 2026-09-09, zero deviations, `reopening: "No"` throughout), with 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-09 in between. A FIFTH AMENDMENT belongs here: the September, October and November ledgers all say '22 consecutive', which does not reconcile with their own 'n=30 constant-size auctions (2024-04-09 -> 2026-09-08, $58,000,000,000 every time)'; the trailing run is 30 and the ramp before it steps 40-42-44-46-48-50-52-54-56 from 2023-07-11 to 2024-03-11. Unlike November, the size DECISION is not in this window — a quarterly refunding statement sets coupon sizes and the December one was set on 2026-11-04, 33 days before this auction; 2026-12-03 merely publishes it. CORRIDOR: 24 tracked entries within +/-5 days, five of them `high` — ISM Services 12-03 and jobs 12-04 land BEFORE the auction, and FOMC 12-09, CPI 12-10 and the government-funding deadline / CR expiry 12-11 all land AFTER it, inside the settlement window. DISCOVERED IN-SWEEP AND PROPOSED IN THIS PR: `treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-03` (this event's own confirming primary), `treasury-10y-note-2026-12-08` and `treasury-30y-bond-2026-12-10` — the block's other two legs, both untracked. NAMED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED, so a sibling can: the January 3-Year new issue (announce 2027-01-07, auction 2027-01-11) and the 12-22 to 12-29 year-end block (5-Year TIPS 12-22, 2-Year FRN and 20-Year 12-23, 2-Year and 5-Year 12-28, 7-Year 12-29). Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
